_rule: A scanned ID autofills the form ONLY when its MRZ is fully self-consistent: every ICAO check digit passes, the CNP's own control digit passes, and the CNP's embedded birth date and sex agree with MRZ line 2. Anything less is rejected and the operator types the fields. A wrong CNP written silently into a client record is worse than no autofill.
_why: TODO-13. The parser is written twice, in two projects, with no shared code and no way to import each other: web/src/features/sales/idScan/mrz.ts and mobile/utils/mrz.ts. This file is what pins that they still AGREE. It is also the only place the accept/reject rule is stated once - each implementation restates it in code, and a case added here fails whichever side does not follow it.

_fields.name: What the case is proving.
_fields.mrz: The OCR output handed to parseMrz, as separate lines. Given verbatim, including the deliberate damage - normalisation and repair are part of what is under test, so the fixture must not pre-clean them.
_fields.accepted: Whether the read may autofill the form.
_fields.fullName: The name the form is filled with, when accepted. Nume then Prenume, title-cased. MRZ is transliterated, so Romanian diacritics are gone and the operator is expected to restore them - this is a suggestion, not a commit.
_fields.cnp: The CNP the form is filled with, or null when the document carries none (a non-Romanian TD1 has no CNP in its optional-data field).
_fields.sex: From MRZ line 2. Not written to the form - EcoTrack stores no sex - but cross-checked against the CNP, which is why it is pinned.
_fields.birthDate: ISO date decoded from the CNP's first seven digits. Null when the CNP is absent, and null for CNP sector digits 7/8/9, where the century is genuinely not encoded. Not written to the form either; pinned because the cross-check depends on decoding it right.
_fields.rejection: Why the read was refused, when it was. 'format' the MRZ is not three 30-character lines; 'check-digit' an ICAO check digit failed; 'cnp-invalid' the CNP's own control digit or county code failed; 'cnp-mismatch' a valid CNP disagrees with the MRZ about birth date or sex.

_provenance: Every MRZ here is synthetic, generated by a separate implementation written before the parser rather than copied from a real card - so the fixture is not a recording of what the TypeScript happens to do, and so no real person's CNP is committed to this repository. The card layout is ICAO 9303 Part 5 TD1; the CNP rules are the Romanian ones (control weights 279146358279, mod 11, 10 to 1).

cases.name: Born after 2000 - sector digit 5, not 1, so the century comes from the CNP and not from the two-digit MRZ year
Non-Romanian TD1 - valid card, empty optional data, so the name autofills and the CNP stays empty
The OCR-B confusion set - 0/O, 1/I, 8/B in numeric fields and 0/O, 1/I in the name - repaired by position and accepted
Whitespace and lower case out of the OCR engine are normalised away, not rejected
The surrounding card text OCR also returns is discarded - the MRZ triple is found inside it
CNP whose control digit is wrong - every ICAO check digit still passes, so the CNP's own checksum is the only thing that catches it
A CNP that is valid on its own but claims a different birth day than MRZ line 2 - caught only by cross-checking the two
A CNP that is valid on its own but says female where MRZ line 2 says male
Document-number check digit fails - the number itself is never used, but a field the parser cannot verify is a field it will not trust the rest of the line beside
Composite check digit fails while every field reads clean - rejected anyway, because something on the card was misread and the parser cannot say what
A line the OCR truncated - not padded back to 30, because padding line 2 would invent the composite check digit that is supposed to catch exactly this
Nothing recognisable at all - a photo of something that is not an ID
